body: A major Microsoft outage has left people around the world unable to use Outlook email, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services since early on Friday morning, Melbourne time.

Problems began at about 4.30am AEDT (12.30pm on Thursday in New York), TechRadar reported. Reports of Outlook problems on the tracking site Downdetector climbed past 120,000 as people found they could not open their inboxes, or send or receive email.

Microsoft's service health page said users might be unable to connect to Exchange Online (Outlook email), Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Copilot for Microsoft 365 and the Defender XDR security service, ABC News reported. Some other companies' tools that connect to Microsoft 365 were also hit.

Microsoft said the problem was not a surge in traffic but "a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable", which put extra load on the rest of its systems, according to the ABC. It paused all updates, moved traffic away from the affected infrastructure and restarted servers. It said it had not found any recent change linked to the start of the problem.

At about 8am AEDT, the Microsoft 365 Status account on X said Microsoft had "validated an alternative service health check method, which allowed a subset of affected servers to successfully return to service", and was applying the fix more widely. TechRadar reported shortly after that the situation was improving.
Microsoft has not said what caused the outage. IT administrators can follow incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin centre.

ul: You don't need to change your password or email settings: the problem is on Microsoft's side.
Emails sent during the outage may arrive late once services recover.
Be wary of emails or texts about the outage asking you to log in or click a link. Scammers often use big outages as cover.
Check Microsoft's service status page or your workplace IT team for updates.

body.note: This is a developing story. Last updated 8.45am AEDT, Friday 13 November.

en.dek: Email, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services went down early on Friday, Melbourne time. Microsoft says a fix is bringing servers back, but has not said what caused it.
en.headline: Microsoft outage knocks out Outlook and Teams worldwide; services starting to recover

body: Parks Victoria has stopped taking new campsite bookings after a data problem at its outside booking provider, Bookeasy, and is warning customers about suspicious WhatsApp messages about their bookings.

In a statement on Wednesday, Parks Victoria said it was working urgently with Bookeasy to understand the issue and was contacting customers who might be affected. Its booking website now shows a "Booking temporarily unavailable" notice.

body.h: What it means if you have a booking

ul: Existing bookings have not been cancelled and are still valid, Parks Victoria says.
You cannot change or modify a booking for now.
New campsite bookings are suspended until further notice.

body: Bookeasy handles camping and vehicle permits for national parks in Victoria, Queensland and South Australia, ABC News reported.

In Queensland, the state's environment department said people's email addresses, home addresses and phone numbers were affected, but it did not believe payment details were accessed because payments run through a separate system. South Australia's National Parks and Wildlife Service said names, contact details and booking information may have been accessed, with no evidence that credit card details were taken. It said Bookeasy had recently detected unauthorised activity and called in cybersecurity experts.
Neither Parks Victoria nor Bookeasy has said what Victorian customers' data was involved, or how many people are affected.

ul: Parks Victoria does not contact customers on WhatsApp.
Do not click links in unexpected messages about a booking.
Do not give payment details or personal information, and do not make a payment in response to a message.
You can report scams at scamwatch.gov.au.

body.note: Check bookings.parks.vic.gov.au for updates on when bookings reopen.

en.dek: Existing bookings still stand, but no new bookings or changes can be made for now. Parks Victoria says it never contacts customers on WhatsApp.
en.headline: Parks Victoria stops campsite bookings after booking provider breach, warns of WhatsApp scams

body: Several long-running disability advocacy services have lost their federal funding as the government replaces a decades-old program with a new one, and a legal service in regional Victoria says it can no longer take on new clients.

Villamanta Disability Rights Legal Service is losing 30 per cent of its total funding, ABC News reported on Thursday. Its chief executive, Annie Nash, told the ABC the cut would mean job losses and less support for people with disability. She said it was hard to understand after a departmental review in March recognised Villamanta as a leader in the sector.

Cherry Baylosis, acting chief executive of Disability Advocacy Network Australia, told the ABC the changes were out of touch with what people with disability need, and warned that people could be left to handle crises alone or families and carers expected to fill the gap.

The Department told the ABC the new funding model responds to recommendations from the disability royal commission. It said up to $184 million, excluding GST, is available over six years from 2026-27 to 2031-32, through an open, competitive grant that both existing and new organisations could apply for.

Services funded under the old program will keep receiving money until February 2027 to help them transition. The changeover takes effect at the end of November. The Department did not say how many organisations had missed out.

The advocacy changes come as the government slows the growth of the National Disability Insurance Scheme. Cuts to therapy funding and to some support worker categories began on 1 October. The government expects about 240,000 participants to leave the scheme over four years, saving more than $38 billion, the ABC reported. The NDIS supports more than 782,000 people and costs more than $50 billion a year.

body.note: If you need help with an NDIS decision, you can ask for an internal review within three months of the decision. Independent advocates can help; the Disability Gateway (1800 643 787) can point you to one.

en.dek: Villamanta Disability Rights Legal Service is losing almost a third of its funding as Canberra replaces a decades-old advocacy program. The Department says the new model follows the disability royal commission.

body: A 17-year-old who went missing while camping in Gippsland has been found alive after six days in rugged bushland east of Melbourne.

William, whose surname has not been released, was found on Thursday morning by a police helicopter crew. ABC News reported that the crew saw his fishing tackle box and then spotted him sleeping in a dry riverbed about 2 kilometres east of Stoney Creek. He was winched to safety.
He had been missing since about 4pm on Friday 6 November, when he was last seen camping with a friend at Walhalla East, about 180 kilometres east of Melbourne.
Police told the ABC that William walked through steep, rocky country and fell down a riverbank two days before he was found. He had left his phone, food and water at a makeshift camp.
He was exhausted and unable to walk, with cuts to his legs and severe sunburn to his face and upper body. He was taken to Latrobe Regional Hospital for monitoring.

Acting Inspector Jason Benbow said William was talking, happy and smiling, and that he "had no idea police were even looking for him", according to the ABC. Inspector Benbow said the terrain was too steep to search on foot, which made the helicopter essential.
His mother, who was at the police staging area at Cowwarr when the news came through, called it "a miracle", the ABC reported.
Police divers, the dog squad and helicopters joined the search, along with SES crews and more than 80 volunteers a day.

body.note: Heading into the bush this summer? Tell someone where you are going and when you will be back, carry water, and stay where you are if you get lost. In an emergency, call Triple Zero (000).

en.dek: A police helicopter crew spotted the 17-year-old asleep in a dry riverbed near Walhalla East. He is sunburnt, cut and exhausted, but talking and smiling, police say.
en.headline: Missing teenager William found alive in Gippsland bush after six days

body: The Greens are aiming to take seats from Labor in Melbourne's inner north and west at the state election on Saturday 28 November, with Northcote shaping as their closest contest, the ABC reported on Tuesday.

The Greens currently hold two lower-house seats, Melbourne and Richmond. Brunswick, which they won in 2022, has been vacant since the death of Greens MP Tim Read, AAP reported. As well as Brunswick, the ABC says the party is targeting the Labor-held seats of Northcote, Preston, Pascoe Vale and Footscray, and the Liberal-held seat of Prahran.

Northcote was held by Lidia Thorpe, now a federal senator, after she won a 2017 by-election. At the 2022 election, Labor's Kat Theophanous held it against Greens candidate Campbell Gome by 184 votes, the ABC said. Both are standing again.

Mr Gome told the ABC's 7.30 program that voters kept telling him Labor had "abandoned communities like ours". Ms Theophanous said she expected another close result and rejected that claim, telling the program: "I don't think we've abandoned ordinary people."
The Victorian Socialists are also running in Northcote. Their candidate, Kath Larkin, told the ABC she did not expect to win but that the party's votes could be decisive in where preferences flow.

ul: The ABC reports Labor holds 54 of the 88 lower-house seats, the Coalition 29, and five sit on the crossbench.
The ABC says recent Redbridge and DemosAU polls put the Greens' statewide primary vote between 14 and 17 per cent, after Labor replaced Jacinta Allan with Ben Carroll as premier.
1,037 candidates are standing across the state, according to the Victorian Electoral Commission.

body: Several of the seats the Greens are targeting, including Footscray, Pascoe Vale and Preston, are home to sizeable migrant communities, so preference flows there could shape the result for many readers.

body.note: Voting is compulsory for enrolled Victorians aged 18 and over. Check who is standing in your district on the VEC website. Reporting in this story draws on the ABC's coverage.

en.dek: The Greens are targeting Northcote, Preston, Pascoe Vale and Footscray at the 28 November election. In Northcote, 184 votes decided the seat last time.

body: A total of 1,037 candidates will contest the Victorian state election on Saturday 28 November, the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC) announced on Tuesday.
Nominations closed at 12 noon on Monday 9 November. The VEC says 734 candidates are standing for the Legislative Assembly (lower house) and 303 for the Legislative Council (upper house).
The commission has also held ballot draws for all 88 lower-house districts and all eight upper-house regions, which set the order in which candidates' names appear on ballot papers.

ul: The VEC lists every candidate on its website. Look up your district (lower house) and your region (upper house).
If you are not sure which district you live in, the VEC's electoral boundaries pages let you search by address.
The VEC has voting information in many community languages, including Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil and Gujarati, on its 'information in your language' page.

body: Staff at the Malmsbury Youth Justice Centre in central Victoria were paid almost $7 million in compensation over violent incidents at work, according to Department of Justice data released to the ABC under freedom of information laws.

The data covers January 2020 to December 2023, when the centre closed after riots and escapes. Over that period, an occupational violence incident was logged every 2.6 days on average, the ABC reported.

One former worker, Justin White, told the ABC he was attacked by detainees armed with a plastic cricket bat in October 2019, a few weeks into the job, and has not been able to work since. "I genuinely thought I wasn't going to come out of it," he said.

The government reopened Malmsbury in April 2026, first with 30 beds and later adding 45. Youth Justice Minister Ros Spence told Nationals MP Gaelle Broad in parliament that, as of 9 September, 22 young people were held there and more than 150 staff were employed.

Ms Spence said operations were being scaled up in stages so the department could recruit and train staff and "stress test operating processes". The department's annual report puts the capital works budget for the reopening at $17.6 million, the ABC reported.
As of 2 November, Victoria's youth justice facilities were at 63.5 per cent of combined capacity, with about 224 young people detained across three sites, the ABC reported.

Youth justice and crime are issues in the campaign for the 28 November state election. Labor has pledged to introduce rehabilitation detention for low and mid-level youth offenders, including at Malmsbury. The Coalition has promised 1,500 more police on top of Labor's recruitment target, and the Greens have called for more spending on mental health, drug and alcohol treatment and youth programs, as we reported in our story on Victoria's prisons.
en.dek: Department of Justice figures released under freedom of information show a violent incident was logged every 2.6 days on average before the centre closed in 2023.

body: Federation University says it is not cutting 87 per cent of its arts subjects, after some staff were told in late October that the subjects would go, the ABC reported on Tuesday 10 November.

Staff at that meeting were also told the Bachelor of Criminal Justice would be cut at every campus except Berwick, according to the ABC. The university has called the meeting a "miscommunication", and the ABC understands it was not authorised by management.

In a statement reported by the ABC, a university spokesperson said Federation was "reviewing courses and units with low student numbers", but that humanities, social work and visual arts "remain important parts of Federation's teaching offering". The spokesperson pointed to the federal government's Job-ready Graduates policy, which raised student contributions for many humanities courses.

Staff across the university's campuses walked off the job for 24 hours on Monday 9 November after eight months of enterprise agreement negotiations failed to produce a deal, the ABC reported. More than 50 staff walked off at the Ballarat campus.

The National Tertiary Education Union says staff want a better pay offer, job security, fair workloads and a say in future decisions. Mathew Abbott, a senior lecturer in humanities and president of the union's Federation branch, told the ABC staff "were given just hours to make submissions" on the proposed cuts, and that the union had lodged a formal complaint.
The ABC reported that further work stoppages are planned for the week starting 16 November, which staff said could delay students receiving grades and results.

body.note: Federation University has campuses in Ballarat, Berwick, Gippsland, Melbourne and the Wimmera. If you are a student worried about your results or course, contact the university's student services directly.

en.dek: Some staff were told 87 per cent of arts subjects would go. The university now calls that a miscommunication, while its union pushes on with industrial action.

body: Residents of Bupa aged care homes who want a cooked breakfast are being asked to sign up for a dining package costing about $42 a day, or $15,330 a year, the ABC has reported.

Residents who do not pay get a continental breakfast, according to the ABC. The package includes two hot breakfasts a week, an extra hot lunch choice each day, a lunch dessert, and a beer, wine or soft drink with lunch and dinner.
Bupa has more than 5,000 aged care residents across Australia, and the ABC reported that thousands could be affected.

Bupa told the ABC it would "provide additional cooked protein options for residents if recommended by a dietitian", whether or not they had chosen its enhanced dining option. In a statement, the company said: "We work hard to provide a consistently high standard of care and services to all our residents."

The charge falls under Higher Everyday Living Fees, or HELF, introduced as part of the federal government's aged care overhaul. HELF lets providers charge residents for optional extra services. The Weekly Source, an aged care industry publication, reported that Bupa's package is within the government's rules.

Aged Care Minister Sam Rae has said the government will change the rules so providers cannot charge a HELF for services that were already part of residents' care before 1 November 2025. The fee is meant for "optional, additional services people choose to receive", his statement says.

The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission told the ABC the law "does not prescribe particular foods, such as cooked eggs". It said it would review the information the ABC provided and assess whether further enquiries were needed.
Dietitians Australia president Fiona Willer told the ABC that many providers do not have dietitians on staff, and that it was not acceptable an egg at breakfast was "now seen as a luxury".

body.note: If you are unsure about a fee charged to a family member in aged care, ask the provider for the written agreement, and raise concerns with the provider or the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission. This is general information, not legal or financial advice.

en.dek: Residents who don't sign up get a continental breakfast. Bupa says dietitian-recommended cooked protein is available to everyone.

body: Workers earning about $45,000 a year, and those approaching the top tax bracket, stand to lose the biggest share of future pay rises to 'bracket creep', according to research released on Wednesday by the e61 Institute, an independent economic research centre.
Bracket creep happens because income tax thresholds are not adjusted for inflation. As wages rise, more of each dollar is taxed at higher rates, even when a pay rise only keeps up with prices.

The research note, by Michael Brennan, Richard Holden, Greg Kaplan, Matthew Maltman and Matt Nolan, models the decade from 2027–28 on the assumption that there are no further income tax cuts. It includes changes already legislated.

ul: The average worker's effective tax rate rises from 20.5 per cent in 2027–28 to 24.1 per cent in 2037–38, assuming real income growth of 1.2 per cent a year.
By 2034–35, tax rates rise by more than 2 percentage points for everyone earning more than $21,000 (in 2025 dollars), except the top 1 per cent.
The largest rise, more than 5 percentage points, is for people earning around $45,000.
For someone on about $45,000, 56 per cent of real income gains would go in extra tax. For someone near $190,000, around the top tax threshold, it would be 65 per cent.

body: "Bracket creep is neither an equitable nor a credible mechanism for restoring fiscal balance," the authors write.

body.h: Why it matters for the budget

body: The federal budget's projected return to surplus relies heavily on bracket creep, the note says. ABC News reported that the Parliamentary Budget Office estimates the budget would show a deficit of 0.7 per cent of GDP by the end of the decade without it, rather than the projected surplus of 1 per cent.
A decade with no tax cuts is unlikely in practice, the ABC noted, because governments have historically cut income tax every few years.

Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has promised to index tax brackets to inflation if the Coalition wins government, phased in from 2028, the ABC reported. Labor has said the plan would force unspecified and damaging spending cuts. Economist Saul Eslake told the ABC he supports indexation in principle but doubts spending cuts of the size needed are achievable.

body.note: This story explains published research. It is general information, not financial or tax advice.

en.dek: Without tax cuts, people on about $45,000 and those near the top tax bracket would lose more than half of their real pay growth to tax over a decade, the e61 Institute says.
en.headline: Pay rises on $45,000 a year will be hit hardest by 'bracket creep', research finds

body: AI companies could face criminal prosecution in Australia if their systems cause harm and they have not taken reasonable steps to prevent it, under an option the federal government is now considering.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the government's response on Tuesday to a review of an incident in which an AI agent made by OpenAI accessed a Medicare statistics website, the ABC and SBS reported.

SBS reported that the government had accepted all 18 recommendations of the rapid review. They include new mandatory safeguards for AI companies operating in Australia, an AI safety regulator to enforce them, mandatory reporting of AI security breaches and of potential breaches of criminal law, and independent evaluation of the most advanced AI models.

According to the ABC, one recommendation was to consider options to reform the criminal law to improve AI safety, and another was to consider criminal penalties for egregious breaches of AI safety standards. The ABC reported the government says the new offence would make Australia the first country to prosecute AI companies on this basis, and that the regulator could issue significant fines. No fine amounts have been given.
SBS reported that the AI agent accessed the Medicare statistics website in June, and that OpenAI informed federal authorities in September.

The ABC reported that a letter from the Australian Federal Police to a parliamentary inquiry, released last week, said the AFP had received no formal report of a crime and had not opened a criminal investigation. Mr Albanese did not say whether he believed OpenAI had committed a crime, and described the hack as "minor in terms of direct implications".

"Australia is a first mover in this space, and we want to make sure that we reap the potential benefits of AI," Mr Albanese told reporters in Canberra, SBS reported. "But we need to ensure that we get it right, and social licence is absolutely critical."
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told the ABC: "It should never be the case that there's an argument that someone didn't know the computer was loaded."

body.h: Experts question how it would work

body: Legal experts quoted by the ABC were cautious. Monash University associate professor Michael Duffy pointed to "problems of proof, working out if harms were foreseeable and proving fault". UTS industry professor Ed Santow said: "I think what will be much more useful is the civil one."
The ABC reported that Italy already has a criminal offence for high-risk AI uses that lack required safeguards, but no one has been prosecuted under it.
OpenAI told the ABC it was reviewing the proposals. The government's AI standards are expected by the end of the year, the ABC reported.

body.note: The Melbourne Indian uses AI tools, including Anthropic's Claude, to help research and draft stories. Anthropic was one of the AI companies the ABC contacted for comment; the ABC reported it did not respond.

en.dek: The federal government says it has accepted every recommendation of a review into the OpenAI incident, and is considering what it calls a world-first offence for AI companies.
en.headline: AI companies could face criminal charges in Australia after an AI agent breached a Medicare website

body: The value of new home loans across Australia fell 15.5 per cent in the September quarter, the largest quarterly fall since the Australian Bureau of Statistics series began in 2002, figures released on Wednesday show.
About 111,900 new home loans worth $81.2 billion were taken out in the three months to September, down 15 per cent in number on the June quarter.

Loans to investors fell 30.6 per cent in number and 32.3 per cent in value, the largest quarterly falls on record for both measures, the ABS said. It was the third quarter in a row of falls, and investor lending dropped in every state and territory.

"While lending activity fell across all borrower types in the September quarter, the decline was sharpest for investors," said Dr Mish Tan, the ABS head of finance statistics. "Our data suggests that investor activity is being influenced by factors beyond increasing borrowing costs."
J.P. Morgan economist Tom Ryan told the ABC that tax changes for investment properties announced in the federal budget had "likely exacerbated the decline".
Loans to owner-occupiers fell 5.3 per cent in number. In Victoria the fall was 6.6 per cent, compared with 10.4 per cent in Queensland and 4.1 per cent in New South Wales.
The number of loans to first home buyers fell 8.6 per cent in the quarter and was 12.3 per cent lower than a year earlier. First home buyers still made up more than a third of owner-occupier loans.
Housing Minister Clare O'Neil told Seven's Sunrise program, as reported by AAP: "What we're seeing is that more first home buyers are winning auctions that they're competing in."

Melbourne home values fell 0.8 per cent in October, the smallest fall of the five biggest cities, according to property data firm Cotality, AAP reported. Cotality's head of research, Gerard Burg, said affordability and investor policies were likely to remain constraints on the market.

body.note: This is general information, not financial advice. If you are thinking about buying, speak to a licensed lender or broker about your own situation.

en.dek: Investor lending dropped by almost a third in the September quarter. First home buyer loans fell too, but buyers still made up more than a third of owner-occupier loans.
en.headline: New home loans suffer their biggest quarterly fall on record, led by investors pulling back

body: Macquarie Bank has admitted it failed to make sure the advertising for its savings account "Welcome Rate" was clear, and faces a proposed $14 million penalty, the corporate regulator ASIC said on Wednesday.
ASIC and Macquarie have jointly proposed the penalty to the NSW Supreme Court, which must still approve it.

Between December 2021 and September 2022, Macquarie advertised a four-month Welcome Rate for new savings customers, describing it as a "bonus". ASIC alleged customers could have thought it was paid on top of the standard variable rate. In fact, it generally replaced the standard rate.
As interest rates rose in 2022, the gap between the two rates shrank or disappeared. Where the standard rate rose above the Welcome Rate, customers simply received the standard rate.
Macquarie admitted breaching the Corporations Act. It had already paid $8.8 million to nearly 40,000 customers, ASIC said.
"Banks must get the basics right," ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland said.

In its statement, Macquarie said some of the wording on its website "was not sufficiently clear". "We apologise for any confusion caused," said Ben Perham, its head of banking and financial services. Macquarie said ASIC had acknowledged the conduct was not deliberate, and that it is reviewing its product descriptions.

In a separate warning, ASIC said Australians may be missing out on interest they were promised, because welcome, introductory and bonus rates often come with conditions or time limits. An ACCC inquiry found that in the first half of 2023, on average 71 per cent of bonus interest accounts did not get the bonus rate each month.
"If you have met the conditions for a higher rate but aren't receiving it, raise it with your bank," Mr Kirkland said.
ASIC suggests checking:

ul: the interest rate you are actually being paid
whether an advertised rate is introductory, promotional or conditional
what you must do each month to get the higher rate, such as deposits, no withdrawals or a minimum balance
how long a promotional rate lasts, and the rate that applies after it ends
whether another account offers a better rate or simpler conditions

body.note: ASIC's Moneysmart website has a guide to savings accounts. If your bank does not fix a problem, you can complain to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). This is general information, not financial advice.

en.dek: Nearly 40,000 customers have already been paid $8.8 million. The regulator says anyone on a bonus or introductory rate should check they are getting what they were promised.
en.headline: Macquarie Bank faces $14 million penalty over its savings 'Welcome Rate', as ASIC tells savers to check their interest

body: Victorian Labor says it will introduce Clare's Law, a scheme that lets people ask police whether a partner has a history of family violence, if it is re-elected on 28 November.

Premier Ben Carroll and Attorney-General Sonya Kilkenny announced the pledge on Tuesday in Fraser Rise, in Melbourne's north-west, the ABC reported. "You deserve to know if your partner has a secret violent past," Mr Carroll said.

ul: A family violence disclosure scheme modelled on South Australia's, which has run since 2018. People could also ask about the partner of a family member or friend they think is at risk, and AAP reports police could share information with people they believe are in danger.
A new criminal offence for people convicted of family violence or sexual offences to use dating apps.

A wider ban on smart glasses, extending to swimming pools, change rooms, community sports venues, hospitals, aged care and family violence services. Smart glasses are already being banned in schools, kindergartens and childcare.
$15.5 million more for The Orange Door, which Labor says would help an extra 10,000 victim-survivors, and $16 million for a new Early Intervention and Prevention Fund.
Power for coroners to appoint an alternative next of kin in cases involving family violence allegations, charges or estrangement.

body: The opposition promised in July to introduce a domestic violence disclosure scheme within 100 days if it wins government, according to the ABC and AAP. AAP reported that Labor voted down a similar Coalition private member's bill in November 2024.
Asked why Labor had not acted sooner, Ms Kilkenny said the government had consulted the family violence sector, and criticised "promises made by the opposition without consulting with the sector".
No start date for the scheme was given.

body.note: If you or someone you know is affected by family violence, call 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or Safe Steps on 1800 015 188, any time. In an emergency, call 000.

en.dek: Victorians could ask police whether a partner has a history of family violence under a scheme both major parties now say they will bring in.
en.headline: Labor promises Clare's Law and a dating-app ban for violent offenders if re-elected

body: A serious form of alcohol-related liver disease is sending younger Victorians and a growing number of women to hospital, according to a new report released on Thursday.

The report, by the Burnet Institute and commissioned by the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education (FARE), looked at Victorian hospital admissions for alcohol-associated hepatitis, a severe inflammation of the liver, from 2017 to mid-2024.

ul: About 40 per cent of people admitted to hospital with alcohol-associated hepatitis were under their mid-40s.
Women now make up about one in three cases.
Admissions rose sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic and remain above pre-pandemic levels. FARE says male admissions are more than double their pre-COVID rate.
The ABC reported that about 13 per cent of patients needed intensive care and the condition had a 4 per cent mortality rate.

body: Professor Jessica Howell, who leads the Burnet Institute's hepatitis and liver cancer research group and is a gastroenterologist at St Vincent's Hospital, said in FARE's release that "women are catching up to men in terms of liver-related harms from alcohol".
She told the ABC the liver can recover if drinking stops early: "We know that the liver can regenerate very well."
FARE chief executive Ayla Chorley said: "This data tells us that reducing alcohol use significantly reduces harm."

ul: Australia's guidelines recommend no more than 10 standard drinks a week and no more than four on any one day.
If you are worried about your own or a family member's drinking, start with your GP.
DirectLine (1800 888 236) offers free, confidential alcohol and drug counselling in Victoria, 24 hours a day. For an interpreter, call TIS National on 131 450.

body.note: This is general health information. Speak to a doctor about your own situation.

en.dek: A Burnet Institute report for the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education found about four in ten hospital admissions for alcohol-associated hepatitis were people under their mid-40s.
en.headline: Severe alcohol-related liver disease is hitting younger Victorians and more women, report finds

body: Borrowers with a variable home loan at any of the big four banks will pay more from Friday 13 November, when the banks lift their variable rates by 0.25 percentage points.

The rises follow the Reserve Bank's decision on 3 November to increase the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85 per cent. Commonwealth Bank, NAB, ANZ and Westpac each announced the following day that they would pass on the full increase, all from 13 November.

ANZ said the rise adds about $79 a month to principal-and-interest repayments on a $500,000 owner-occupier variable loan. The exact change for any household depends on the loan size, the rate and the time left on the loan. Banks usually write to customers with their new repayment amount.

dl: Variable home loan rates up 0.25 percentage points from 13 November. The bank's release did not mention savings rates.
Variable home loan rates up 0.25 percentage points from 13 November. NAB said it regularly reviews savings rates but announced no change.
Variable home loan rates up 0.25 percentage points from 13 November. The bonus rate on its ANZ Plus Growth Saver also rises 0.25 points, to a total of 5.60 per cent.
Variable home loan rates up 0.25 percentage points from 13 November, for new and existing customers. The Westpac Life total variable rate with bonus interest rises to 5.50 per cent.

body: All four banks urged customers who are struggling to get in touch early. "If things are getting tight, please don't wait until you're struggling to make a repayment," said NAB's Ana Marinkovic. CBA's Angus Sullivan said: "For customers who may be concerned about their financial position, we encourage them to contact us early."

In its November Statement on Monetary Policy, the Reserve Bank said headline inflation was 3.9 per cent in the year to the September quarter. It expects inflation "to remain above 3 per cent until late 2027, reflecting recent increases in fuel and other conflict-related costs and greater domestic capacity pressures". The Board said it "will continue to do what it considers necessary to bring inflation sustainably back to target".

body.h: If you are worried about repayments

ul: Call your lender before you miss a payment. Banks have hardship teams and must consider requests for help.
Check whether your rate is still competitive: a lender or a licensed mortgage broker can compare options.
The National Debt Helpline (1800 007 007) gives free, confidential financial counselling. Interpreters are available through TIS National on 131 450.

body.note: This story explains announced rate changes. It is general information, not financial advice. Check your own loan with your lender or a licensed adviser.

en.dek: CBA, NAB, ANZ and Westpac are lifting variable home loan rates by 0.25 percentage points from 13 November, after the Reserve Bank raised the cash rate to 4.85 per cent.

body: Councillor Abhishek Awasthi has been elected Mayor of the City of Greater Bendigo for 2026-27, the council announced this week.
Councillors chose Cr Awasthi at a meeting at Bendigo's Capital Theatre on Monday night. Cr Andrea Metcalf was elected Deputy Mayor. They replace Cr Thomas Prince and Cr Karen Corr.
The Indian Sun reported that Cr Awasthi is the first person of Indian origin to be mayor of Greater Bendigo. He was deputy mayor in 2024-25, serving alongside Cr Metcalf when she was mayor.

Cr Awasthi represents Kennington Ward and was first elected to council in November 2024. According to his council profile, he has lived in Greater Bendigo since 2010, lives in Kennington with his wife and daughter, and volunteers with the CFA's Bendigo Fire Brigade.

The Indian Sun reported that he is originally from Mandi in Himachal Pradesh, came to Australia in 2008 to study biotechnology at La Trobe University, and became an Australian citizen in 2015. It said his parents and relatives attended the meeting.

In the council's announcement, Cr Awasthi said he was honoured by his colleagues' confidence. "Listening to our community will remain at the heart of my approach," he said, adding: "Small businesses are the lifeblood of our local economy."
His council profile lists his priorities as strong governance, economic development and building partnerships across the community.
Cr Metcalf said affordable housing, community partnerships, active transport and tackling illegal dumping were among her priorities.
en.dek: The Kennington Ward councillor, who came to Australia from Himachal Pradesh to study, will lead the regional city for the next year. The Indian Sun reports he is its first mayor of Indian origin.
en.headline: Abhishek Awasthi elected Mayor of Greater Bendigo

body: पार्षद अभिषेक अवस्थी को 2026-27 के लिए सिटी ऑफ़ ग्रेटर बेंडिगो का मेयर चुना गया है। सोमवार रात कैपिटल थिएटर में हुई बैठक में पार्षदों ने उन्हें चुना। पार्षद एंड्रिया मेटकाफ़ उप-मेयर बनीं।
द इंडियन सन के अनुसार वे ग्रेटर बेंडिगो के पहले भारतीय मूल के मेयर हैं। वे 2024-25 में उप-मेयर रह चुके हैं।

काउंसिल के अनुसार वे 2010 से ग्रेटर बेंडिगो में रहते हैं और CFA की बेंडिगो फ़ायर ब्रिगेड में स्वयंसेवक हैं। द इंडियन सन के अनुसार वे हिमाचल प्रदेश के मंडी से हैं और 2008 में ला ट्रोब विश्वविद्यालय में पढ़ने आए थे।
काउंसिल की घोषणा में उन्होंने कहा कि समुदाय की बात सुनना उनके काम का केंद्र रहेगा और छोटे व्यवसाय स्थानीय अर्थव्यवस्था की जीवनरेखा हैं।

body: ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਅਭਿਸ਼ੇਕ ਅਵਸਥੀ ਨੂੰ 2026-27 ਲਈ ਸਿਟੀ ਆਫ਼ ਗ੍ਰੇਟਰ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਦਾ ਮੇਅਰ ਚੁਣਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਸੋਮਵਾਰ ਰਾਤ ਕੈਪੀਟਲ ਥੀਏਟਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੋਈ ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੌਂਸਲਰਾਂ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਚੁਣਿਆ। ਕੌਂਸਲਰ ਐਂਡਰੀਆ ਮੈਟਕਾਫ਼ ਡਿਪਟੀ ਮੇਅਰ ਬਣੇ।
ਦ ਇੰਡੀਅਨ ਸਨ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਹ ਗ੍ਰੇਟਰ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਦੇ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਮੂਲ ਦੇ ਮੇਅਰ ਹਨ। ਉਹ 2024-25 ਵਿੱਚ ਡਿਪਟੀ ਮੇਅਰ ਰਹਿ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ।

ਕੌਂਸਲ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਹ 2010 ਤੋਂ ਗ੍ਰੇਟਰ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ CFA ਦੀ ਬੈਂਡਿਗੋ ਫ਼ਾਇਰ ਬ੍ਰਿਗੇਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਲੰਟੀਅਰ ਹਨ। ਦ ਇੰਡੀਅਨ ਸਨ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਹ ਹਿਮਾਚਲ ਪ੍ਰਦੇਸ਼ ਦੇ ਮੰਡੀ ਤੋਂ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ 2008 ਵਿੱਚ ਲਾ ਟ੍ਰੋਬ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੜ੍ਹਨ ਆਏ ਸਨ।
ਕੌਂਸਲ ਦੇ ਐਲਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਭਾਈਚਾਰੇ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਸੁਣਨਾ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਦਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਰਹੇਗਾ ਅਤੇ ਛੋਟੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰ ਸਥਾਨਕ ਅਰਥਚਾਰੇ ਦੀ ਜੀਵਨ-ਰੇਖਾ ਹਨ।

body: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has taken the Commonwealth Bank to the Federal Court, alleging it overcharged about 42,000 business customers roughly $8.5 million in fees they were not told about.
The civil penalty case was filed late on Wednesday and concerns CommBiz, CBA's online banking platform for businesses, according to reports by the ABC and AAP.

ASIC says the CommBiz terms and conditions told customers they would pay a fee for direct debit and direct credit payments to or from a third party's account. It alleges CBA also charged a second fee, which was not disclosed, for the matching movement of money into or out of the customer's own CommBiz account.
The ABC reported ASIC's example: a business paying wages to 10 employees from two accounts was charged 12 fees, two of them undisclosed.

The case covers fees charged between November 2020 and May 2025. But ASIC alleges the misleading terms had been in place for about 19 years, since CommBiz launched in 2006, that the bank received complaints about the fees from at least 2015, and that a 2016 internal audit found direct debit fees were being overcharged.
"We allege Commonwealth Bank broke a basic promise to its business customers," ASIC commissioner Alan Kirkland said. "Small businesses are busy enough."
ASIC is seeking declarations, financial penalties, adverse publicity orders and costs. The court has not yet set a date for the first hearing.

In a statement to the ASX reported by the ABC, CBA said it had identified the problem itself, reported it to ASIC and cooperated fully. It said the issue came from simplified terms that did not accurately describe how the fee, 25 cents plus GST, was charged. The bank said it "accepts that it did not get things right for CommBiz customers" and apologised, but disputes how some allegations are framed. It said it would defend parts of the claim or keep working with ASIC to resolve it.

CBA stopped charging the fees in June 2025 and changed the terms that August. It says a remediation program covering December 2006 onwards has already paid more than $26.4 million to about 93,000 customers, including about 40,000 small businesses.

ul: CBA says its remediation program is complete. If you think you were affected and have not heard from the bank, contact CBA directly.
If you are not satisfied with the bank's answer, the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) handles complaints from small businesses for free: afca.org.au or 1800 931 678.

body.note: These are allegations made by ASIC in civil proceedings. They have not been tested in court.

en.dek: The corporate regulator says CBA's CommBiz terms did not disclose a second fee on direct debits and credits. The bank says it found the problem itself and has already repaid more than $26 million.
en.headline: ASIC sues Commonwealth Bank, alleging it overcharged 42,000 business customers $8.5 million in hidden fees

body: Victorian Labor has promised $420 million to run more than 550 extra V/Line trips a week if it wins the state election on 28 November, with the largest increases on the lines through Melbourne's fast-growing west.
Premier Ben Carroll announced the plan on Thursday. Labor says it would grow regional train services by about a quarter, according to reports by the ABC and AAP.

body.h: What would change, line by line

ul: Wyndham Vale: 249 extra trips a week from 2027, on a dedicated service meant to ease crowding. Trains to Wyndham Vale also stop at Tarneit.
Melton: 162 extra trips a week from 2027, so trains run every 20 minutes. Longer nine-car trains, announced earlier, are also due next year.
Bendigo line: 101 extra trips a week from 2028, including 80 new services to Kyneton and 21 more to Bendigo.
Seymour line (through Donnybrook and Wallan): 29 extra trips a week from 2028, with trains every 40 minutes between peaks instead of hourly.
Geelong: more express services that cut about 10 minutes from the trip, and two extra Sunday services to Geelong and Waurn Ponds.
Ballarat: most weekday off-peak trains to run express to Melbourne from next year.
Warrnambool: eight extra weekend services from next year. Traralgon: one extra Sunday service from 2028.

body: AAP reported that new hybrid electric trains on the Melton and Wyndham Vale lines would free up 25 three-car V/Line trains for use elsewhere. Mr Carroll told AAP the new services would let Victorians "realise the benefits of Labor's upgrades".

The ABC said the pledge targets regional and outer-suburban seats where Labor is under pressure from the Coalition and One Nation. AAP reported that a poll by RedBridge and Accent Research for the Australian Financial Review, published on Wednesday, put the Coalition's primary vote at 31 per cent, Labor at 23, One Nation at 22 and the Greens at 15.

In September the Coalition promised to back more train capacity across the state, and it has pledged $1.7 billion for hybrid trains to Melton and Wyndham Vale, the ABC reported. The government has questioned whether that plan could work alongside the rest of the network.

body.h: A fight over the Liberals' surplus plan

body: Labor also released analysis it had asked the Parliamentary Budget Office to do on Liberal leader Jess Wilson's promise of a cash surplus by 2032, the ABC reported. Ms Wilson's plan relies mostly on shrinking the public service through attrition, which she says would save $22 billion over a decade.

According to the ABC, the budget office estimated the policy would save $8.5 billion by 2032, with most of the savings arriving later. Treasurer Colin Brooks said this showed a Wilson government would have to cut services such as health.

Ms Wilson said in a statement she would not take lectures on costings from Labor. "Only our Liberal and Nationals team has a costed and credible plan to repair the budget," she said, pointing to more than $26 billion in savings. The ABC noted that budget office results depend on the assumptions they are given, and that Ms Wilson has not released her own version of the analysis.

body.note: Election pledges are promises, not funded projects. We report what each party says it will do and link to our sources so you can check.

en.dek: Premier Ben Carroll says more than 550 extra regional trips a week would be added if Labor is re-elected on 28 November. Labor also used a budget office analysis to attack the Liberals' surplus plan.

body: National Australia Bank (NAB) has signed an enforceable undertaking with the Fair Work Ombudsman after underpaying about 66,000 current and former staff between 2012 and this year, AAP reported on Thursday.

The bank has agreed to pay $127 million in wages and entitlements, $34 million in interest and $8 million in superannuation, a total of about $169 million. HR Leader reported that NAB has already paid at least $155 million of it.
NAB will also make a $2 million contrition payment to the Commonwealth, the largest ever included in a Fair Work Ombudsman enforceable undertaking, according to AAP.

NAB reported the underpayments to the Ombudsman itself in late 2019, after finding significant errors in how it applied its enterprise agreement. Further problems were found in 2024 when it brought in a new agreement, HR Leader reported.

ul: Minimum wages for ordinary hours
Penalty rates, shift loadings and overtime
Annual, personal and long service leave
Superannuation

body: The Ombudsman pointed to poor record-keeping, old payroll technology and weak oversight. Fair Work Ombudsman Anna Booth said it was "particularly disappointing to see these types of large and long-running underpayment issues" at such a well-resourced employer, AAP reported.
NAB executive Sarah White said the bank took its payroll obligations "extremely seriously". "We sincerely apologise for these unintended errors," she said, according to AAP.

ul: Pay everyone affected, including for periods outside the usual legal time limits
Hire an independent auditor to check its new payroll system
Set up a steering committee led by a senior executive
Train staff on recording extra hours worked

body.note: If you work or worked at NAB and think you may be owed money, contact NAB or the Fair Work Ombudsman on 13 13 94. Interpreters are available through the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450.

en.dek: The bank reported the problems itself in 2019. Some workers are owed under $5; others more than $87,000. The average is about $1,900.

body: Victorians may not see a free-to-air debate between the people who want to be premier before the state election on 28 November.

The ABC invited the leaders of Labor, the Liberals, One Nation and the Greens last month to a debate broadcast on its TV, radio and digital platforms in Victoria. Labor, the Greens and One Nation accepted, but the Liberals declined, so the debate will not go ahead, the ABC reported on Thursday.

A separate debate proposed by Nine, The Age and the Australian Financial Review, between Premier Ben Carroll and Opposition Leader Jess Wilson with a rebuttal from One Nation leader Warren Pickering, will also not go ahead because the premier did not agree to the format, according to the ABC.

Ms Wilson has argued that only she or Mr Carroll can become premier, so any debate should be between the two of them. Labor argues that One Nation, which it says has the support of between 20 and 25 per cent of voters, deserves a place, the ABC reported.

A Liberal campaign spokesperson told the ABC that "engagement comes in many forms and doesn't always have to be through the media or at organised forums", and that decisions about events were made "on a case-by-case basis".

The only leaders' event the ABC describes as locked in is a town hall hosted by the Herald Sun and News24, with Mr Pickering and Ms Sandell also in the line-up. The ABC did not say whether Mr Carroll and Ms Wilson have confirmed they will take part.

In a media release on Thursday, Ms Sandell called on the other leaders to appear on the ABC. "If you want to lead Victoria, if you want people to vote for you, you should be able to get through an hour of questions without weeks of negotiations about who's allowed in the room," she said.

body.note: Early voting opens on Wednesday 18 November and election day is Saturday 28 November. Our early voting guide lists centres in Tarneit, Point Cook, Cranbourne and four other districts. The Melbourne Indian does not endorse candidates or parties.

en.dek: With 16 days until Victorians vote, the only leaders' event locked in is a Herald Sun and News24 town hall. Greens leader Ellen Sandell says the other leaders should "grow up".
en.headline: No ABC leaders' debate this election after the Liberals decline, and Nine's debate falls through too

body: हो सकता है कि 28 नवंबर के राज्य चुनाव से पहले विक्टोरिया के लोग प्रीमियर पद के दावेदारों के बीच कोई फ़्री-टू-एयर बहस न देख पाएँ।

ABC ने पिछले महीने लेबर, लिबरल, वन नेशन और ग्रीन्स के नेताओं को विक्टोरिया में अपने टीवी, रेडियो और डिजिटल प्लेटफ़ॉर्म पर प्रसारित होने वाली बहस के लिए बुलाया था। ABC ने गुरुवार को बताया कि लेबर, ग्रीन्स और वन नेशन ने न्योता स्वीकार किया, लेकिन लिबरल पार्टी ने इनकार कर दिया, इसलिए यह बहस नहीं होगी।

ABC के अनुसार, Nine, The Age और Australian Financial Review की ओर से प्रस्तावित एक अलग बहस भी नहीं होगी। इसमें प्रीमियर बेन कैरल और विपक्ष की नेता जेस विल्सन आमने-सामने होते, और वन नेशन के नेता वॉरेन पिकरिंग जवाब देते। यह इसलिए रद्द हुई क्योंकि प्रीमियर इस फ़ॉर्मेट पर सहमत नहीं हुए।

body.h: पार्टियाँ सहमत क्यों नहीं हो पा रहीं

body: सुश्री विल्सन का तर्क है कि प्रीमियर सिर्फ़ वे या श्री कैरल ही बन सकते हैं, इसलिए कोई भी बहस इन दोनों के बीच होनी चाहिए। ABC के अनुसार, लेबर का तर्क है कि वन नेशन को जगह मिलनी चाहिए, क्योंकि लेबर के मुताबिक उसे 20 से 25 प्रतिशत मतदाताओं का समर्थन है।
लिबरल अभियान के एक प्रवक्ता ने ABC से कहा कि "जुड़ाव कई तरह से होता है और यह हमेशा मीडिया या आयोजित मंचों के ज़रिए ही ज़रूरी नहीं", और कार्यक्रमों के बारे में फ़ैसले "हर मामले को देखकर" लिए जाते हैं।

ABC के मुताबिक नेताओं का एकमात्र तय कार्यक्रम Herald Sun और News24 का टाउन हॉल है, जिसमें श्री पिकरिंग और सुश्री सैंडेल भी शामिल हैं। ABC ने यह नहीं बताया कि श्री कैरल और सुश्री विल्सन ने इसमें शामिल होने की पुष्टि की है या नहीं।

गुरुवार को जारी एक मीडिया विज्ञप्ति में सुश्री सैंडेल ने बाकी नेताओं से ABC पर आने की अपील की। उन्होंने कहा, "अगर आप विक्टोरिया का नेतृत्व करना चाहते हैं, अगर आप चाहते हैं कि लोग आपको वोट दें, तो आपको हफ़्तों तक यह मोलभाव किए बिना कि कमरे में कौन आ सकता है, एक घंटे के सवालों का सामना करने में सक्षम होना चाहिए।"

body.note: अर्ली वोटिंग बुधवार 18 नवंबर से शुरू होती है और चुनाव का दिन शनिवार 28 नवंबर है। हमारी अर्ली वोटिंग गाइड में टार्नेट, पॉइंट कुक, क्रैनबर्न और चार अन्य क्षेत्रों के केंद्र दिए गए हैं। The Melbourne Indian किसी उम्मीदवार या पार्टी का समर्थन नहीं करता।

hi.dek: विक्टोरिया में मतदान से 16 दिन पहले, नेताओं का एकमात्र तय कार्यक्रम Herald Sun और News24 का टाउन हॉल है। ग्रीन्स नेता एलेन सैंडेल का कहना है कि बाकी नेताओं को "बड़ा होना चाहिए"।

ABC ਨੇ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਮਹੀਨੇ ਲੇਬਰ, ਲਿਬਰਲ, ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਅਤੇ ਗ੍ਰੀਨਜ਼ ਦੇ ਨੇਤਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣੇ ਟੀਵੀ, ਰੇਡੀਓ ਅਤੇ ਡਿਜੀਟਲ ਪਲੇਟਫ਼ਾਰਮਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਿਤ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਬਹਿਸ ਲਈ ਸੱਦਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਸੀ। ABC ਨੇ ਵੀਰਵਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਲੇਬਰ, ਗ੍ਰੀਨਜ਼ ਅਤੇ ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਨੇ ਸੱਦਾ ਸਵੀਕਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ, ਪਰ ਲਿਬਰਲ ਪਾਰਟੀ ਨੇ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ, ਇਸ ਲਈ ਇਹ ਬਹਿਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ।

ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, Nine, The Age ਅਤੇ Australian Financial Review ਵੱਲੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਸਤਾਵਿਤ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਖਰੀ ਬਹਿਸ ਵੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ। ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰੀਮੀਅਰ ਬੈਨ ਕੈਰਲ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਰੋਧੀ ਧਿਰ ਦੀ ਨੇਤਾ ਜੈੱਸ ਵਿਲਸਨ ਆਹਮੋ-ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਹੁੰਦੇ, ਅਤੇ ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਨੇਤਾ ਵਾਰਨ ਪਿਕਰਿੰਗ ਜਵਾਬ ਦਿੰਦੇ। ਇਹ ਇਸ ਲਈ ਰੱਦ ਹੋਈ ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਮੀਅਰ ਇਸ ਫ਼ਾਰਮੈਟ 'ਤੇ ਸਹਿਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਏ।

body.h: ਪਾਰਟੀਆਂ ਸਹਿਮਤ ਕਿਉਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋ ਰਹੀਆਂ

body: ਸ੍ਰੀਮਤੀ ਵਿਲਸਨ ਦੀ ਦਲੀਲ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਮੀਅਰ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਉਹ ਜਾਂ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਕੈਰਲ ਹੀ ਬਣ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ, ਇਸ ਲਈ ਕੋਈ ਵੀ ਬਹਿਸ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਵਿਚਕਾਰ ਹੋਣੀ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ। ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ, ਲੇਬਰ ਦੀ ਦਲੀਲ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਵਨ ਨੇਸ਼ਨ ਨੂੰ ਥਾਂ ਮਿਲਣੀ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ, ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਲੇਬਰ ਦੇ ਕਹਿਣ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ 20 ਤੋਂ 25 ਪ੍ਰਤੀਸ਼ਤ ਵੋਟਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਮਰਥਨ ਹੈ।

ਲਿਬਰਲ ਮੁਹਿੰਮ ਦੇ ਇੱਕ ਬੁਲਾਰੇ ਨੇ ABC ਨੂੰ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ "ਜੁੜਨ ਦੇ ਕਈ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਇਹ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਮੀਡੀਆ ਜਾਂ ਕਰਵਾਏ ਗਏ ਮੰਚਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਹੀ ਹੋਣਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਨਹੀਂ", ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲੇ "ਹਰ ਮਾਮਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਦੇਖ ਕੇ" ਲਏ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

ABC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਨੇਤਾਵਾਂ ਦਾ ਇੱਕੋ-ਇੱਕ ਤੈਅ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ Herald Sun ਅਤੇ News24 ਦਾ ਟਾਊਨ ਹਾਲ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਪਿਕਰਿੰਗ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰੀਮਤੀ ਸੈਂਡੇਲ ਵੀ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹਨ। ABC ਨੇ ਇਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਕੈਰਲ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰੀਮਤੀ ਵਿਲਸਨ ਨੇ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ ਜਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ।

ਵੀਰਵਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਰੀ ਇੱਕ ਮੀਡੀਆ ਬਿਆਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀਮਤੀ ਸੈਂਡੇਲ ਨੇ ਬਾਕੀ ਨੇਤਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ABC 'ਤੇ ਆਉਣ ਦੀ ਅਪੀਲ ਕੀਤੀ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਿਹਾ, "ਜੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਦੀ ਅਗਵਾਈ ਕਰਨਾ ਚਾਹੁੰਦੇ ਹੋ, ਜੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਚਾਹੁੰਦੇ ਹੋ ਕਿ ਲੋਕ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਵੋਟ ਪਾਉਣ, ਤਾਂ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਹਫ਼ਤਿਆਂ ਤੱਕ ਇਸ ਗੱਲ 'ਤੇ ਸੌਦੇਬਾਜ਼ੀ ਕੀਤੇ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਕਿ ਕਮਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੌਣ ਆ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਇੱਕ ਘੰਟੇ ਦੇ ਸਵਾਲਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਾਹਮਣਾ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਯੋਗ ਹੋਣਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ।"

body.note: ਅਰਲੀ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ 18 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਚੋਣ ਦਾ ਦਿਨ ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ 28 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਹੈ। ਸਾਡੀ ਅਰਲੀ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਗਾਈਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਟਾਰਨੇਟ, ਪੁਆਇੰਟ ਕੁੱਕ, ਕ੍ਰੈਨਬਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਚਾਰ ਹੋਰ ਹਲਕਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਗਏ ਹਨ। The Melbourne Indian ਕਿਸੇ ਉਮੀਦਵਾਰ ਜਾਂ ਪਾਰਟੀ ਦਾ ਸਮਰਥਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦਾ।

body: Early voting for the Victorian state election opens on Wednesday 18 November, and the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC) has now published where it will happen.

The VEC's venue list, correct as at 7 November, names 211 early voting centres across the state's 88 districts. They are open from 9am to 6pm every day from Wednesday 18 to Friday 27 November, except Sunday 22 November, when they are closed. You do not need a reason to vote early.
Below are the centres the VEC lists for the seven districts where at least one in 10 residents was born in India. Some centres serve more than one district.

body: The VEC's planning estimates suggest some of these centres will be among the busiest. It expects about 24,000 early votes at Connect City Church West in Hoppers Crossing, about 23,000 at the Salicki Avenue centre in Epping and about 22,000 at the 1st Cranbourne Scout Hall. If you can, avoid the last few days before election day.

The VEC rates every centre for wheelchair access. Several on this list, including Connect City Church West, the 1st Werribee and 1st Cranbourne scout halls and the Yellowbox Drive centre in Craigieburn, are rated as having limited or no wheelchair access. The VEC's venue locator shows the rating and entrance details for each centre.

If you will be overseas, the VEC has voting venues in 30 cities across 21 countries. Its list includes the Australian High Commission in New Delhi for in-person voting and postal vote drop-off. Check the VEC's overseas venue list for opening dates and hours before you go. You can also apply for a postal vote until 6pm on Wednesday 25 November.
Election day is Saturday 28 November, when voting centres are open from 8am to 6pm.

body: The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority (VCAA), which runs VCE exams, confirmed its website was hacked on Wednesday, with about a week of the 2026 exam period still to go.
Around 6pm, a message from someone using the alias "DaggerElite" appeared on the VCAA home page, The Age reported. Later in the evening the site showed only a maintenance notice.
The VCAA said its site had been the "subject of vandalism" and that an initial investigation found no evidence that sensitive data or exam papers had been accessed, according to The Age.

"There is no indication that exam papers from today or previous weeks have been accessed," the authority said, according to the ABC. The VCAA said it was conducting a forensic investigation "to determine the extent of the attack". The Age reported that the authority had referred the incident to Victoria Police. VCE exams are continuing as scheduled.

The message on the home page claimed the hacker had downloaded 2026 exam papers from the VCAA's printing provider, which was not named, and sold copies to students ahead of exam day. It also claimed the papers were emailed using a law firm's address. None of these claims has been verified, and the VCAA's statement contradicts them.

GoAhead Lawyers told The Age it suspected its email address had been spoofed, that it had not authorised any emails distributing VCE papers, that it found no record of them in its systems, and that it had reported the matter to the VCAA.

The Coalition's education spokesperson, Brad Rowswell, has asked for a briefing from the Education Department and the VCAA, according to The Age and Ticker News. The Age reported that Education Minister Gabrielle Williams had been contacted for comment.
The exam period ends with language exams on 18 November, and results are due on 10 December.

The VCAA has had exam problems before. In 2024 it accidentally published material that showed questions from that year's exams, The Age and the ABC reported. In April this year the state government announced more than $222 million to rebuild the authority.

body.note: Students and parents: the VCAA says exams continue as scheduled. Check your school and the VCAA for any official update before your next exam, and do not open or share files claiming to be exam papers.

en.dek: A hacker posted claims on the exam authority's home page that VCE papers had been sold to students. The VCAA says exams will go ahead as normal and has called in police.
en.headline: VCAA website hacked mid-exams, but authority says no sign VCE papers were accessed

body: Students anywhere in Victoria would be able to study Hindi, Punjabi, Bengali or Tamil for VCE, even if their school does not teach it, under a $43 million election promise from Victorian Labor.

Premier Ben Carroll said a re-elected Labor government would expand online classes at the Victorian School of Languages (VSL) from the 17 VCE languages it teaches online now to all 44 modern VCE languages, starting in 2028. Labor also says it will explore adding Sanskrit.

"Learning a language doesn't just help young people stay connected to their past – it can unlock their future," Mr Carroll said. "Every Victorian student should have the opportunity to study the language they want, no matter where they live."
More than 16,000 Victorian students are studying a VCE language this year, and about 800 of them do it through VSL's online classes, according to the announcement.

For families in growth suburbs such as Tarneit, Truganina, Craigieburn and Cranbourne, the practical change is simple: a student whose school offers only French or Japanese could take Hindi or Punjabi online and have it count towards their VCE.

dl: Online VCE classes at the Victorian School of Languages, from 17 languages to all 44

body: Education Minister Gabrielle Williams said the investment would "give more students better access to language education". Mr Carroll added: "Labor will always back our Indian community."

In March, while he was Deputy Premier and Education Minister, Mr Carroll announced $150,000 in scholarships to train 18 Hindi and Punjabi teachers through Monash University, and $3.5 million for three schools to lead the teaching of the two languages: Alkira Secondary College in Cranbourne North and Wyndham Central College in Werribee for Hindi, and Mount Ridley P-12 College in Craigieburn for Punjabi.

Labor contrasted the promise with what it called a "$40 billion cuts agenda" from a "Liberal–One Nation Coalition". The Coalition, led by Jess Wilson, had not responded publicly to the languages pledge when it was announced on 8 November.

body.note: Election day is Saturday 28 November. Early voting opens on Wednesday 18 November.

en.dek: A re-elected Labor government would expand the Victorian School of Languages' online classes from 17 VCE languages to all 44 from 2028, and says it will explore adding Sanskrit.
en.headline: Labor promises $43 million so every VCE student can study Hindi, Punjabi and 42 other languages online

body: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) is checking retailers across several sectors for misleading sales claims in the lead-up to Black Friday on 27 November and Cyber Monday on 30 November.

It is the watchdog's third sweep of the shopping events, and the first to look at promotions in emails and on social media as well as on retailers' websites, the ACCC said on Tuesday. Australians often spend close to $7 billion over the period, SBS News reported.

body.h: What the ACCC is looking for

ul: 'Sitewide' or 'storewide' sales where many products are excluded
Time-limited offers and countdown timers that keep running after the stated end date
Pressure tactics, such as misleading testimonials or false claims that stock is about to run out
Sale prices compared against a 'was' price the product was never, or not recently, sold at

body: "Retailers risk ACCC enforcement action if they misrepresent the size, scope or duration of their sales," ACCC deputy chair Catriona Lowe said. "Retailers should not be relying on fine print disclaimers or exclusions to qualify the headline message of a promotion."

Earlier sweeps led to penalties. Michael Hill, My House and Hairhouse Warehouse Online paid penalties in June 2025 over alleged misleading sitewide claims, and digiDirect, James Lane and Vuly paid penalties in September this year, the ACCC said.

In the first nine months of 2026, 58.7 per cent of Scamwatch reports involving a financial loss were about buying and selling scams, the ACCC said. It warned shoppers to be wary of fake online shops that use big discounts and 'limited time' pressure to rush people into paying.

ul: Focus on the final price you will pay, not the promotional headline
Read the exclusions and conditions before you buy
Compare prices across retailers and against the product's past prices
Buy only if the price and timing suit you, not because a timer is counting down
Check you are dealing with a legitimate seller

body: "Consumers should be aware that a 'sale' sign doesn't always mean it's a good deal," Ms Lowe said.

body.note: To report a misleading sale, use the ACCC's consumer issue form at accc.gov.au. Report scams to Scamwatch.

en.dek: The consumer watchdog's third Black Friday sweep will, for the first time, check retailers' emails and social media as well as their websites. Here is what it is looking for, and how to shop safely.
en.headline: Black Friday sales: the ACCC is watching for fake 'storewide' deals and countdown timers

body: A 27-year-old woman has been charged with trafficking heroin and methylamphetamine after detectives searched a unit in Mordialloc, in Melbourne's south-east, Victoria Police says.

Detectives from the Moorabbin Crime Investigation Unit executed a search warrant at the Crown Avenue unit at about 6.45am on Tuesday 10 November. Police say they found traffickable quantities of heroin and methylamphetamine, a hatchet, and items consistent with selling drugs. The release did not give the amounts.
Two women, aged 27 and 36, were arrested at the scene.

ul: Trafficking heroin and methylamphetamine
Possessing a controlled weapon
Dealing with property suspected of being proceeds of crime
Contravening bail

body: The 27-year-old appeared at Moorabbin Magistrates' Court on Tuesday and was remanded in custody to reappear on 4 December, police said. The 36-year-old was released and police intend to charge her on summons. Police did not name either woman.
Police say enquiries are continuing.

body.note: Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or at crimestoppersvic.com.au. You can stay anonymous. Charges are allegations that have not been tested in court.

en.dek: Detectives say they found traffickable quantities of both drugs, a hatchet and drug paraphernalia at a unit on Crown Avenue on Tuesday morning.
en.headline: Woman charged with trafficking heroin and methylamphetamine after police raid in Mordialloc

body: RAAF Williams at Point Cook, Victoria Barracks on St Kilda Road and Fort Queenscliff will not be sold, after the federal government reversed part of its plan to sell surplus Defence land.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the change on Sunday at Victoria Barracks in Sydney, which will also stay in public hands. The ABC reported that the three Victorian sites will move from Defence to the Department of Finance rather than be sold.

Wyndham Mayor Mia Shaw said on Monday the council "welcomes the announcement that RAAF Williams will no longer be considered for sale". She said the site "should never have been considered as surplus land" and was "one of the most important aviation heritage sites in Australia". The council had made submissions to the federal government against the sale.

An audit in February identified 67 Defence sites for sale, which were expected to raise $1.8 billion, the ABC reported. Defence Minister Richard Marles said: "It is utterly untenable to be spending hundreds of millions of dollars on Defence sites" that Defence does not need.
Opposition defence spokesman James Paterson called the decision "a huge victory for the community", but said: "It's very difficult to see how the government's budget numbers now add up."

RSL Australia said more than 60 other sites were still earmarked for sale and asked the government to pause them until a Senate inquiry into Defence estate assets reports. "There's no undo button. Once a site is sold, it's gone for good," the RSL said.
en.dek: Wyndham's mayor welcomed the backdown on RAAF Williams, one of the country's most important aviation heritage sites. More than 60 other Defence sites are still earmarked for sale.
en.headline: Point Cook air base and Victoria Barracks in Melbourne taken off Defence's sale list

body: The Victorian Liberal Party has withdrawn its endorsement of Paul Lindemann, its candidate for the Labor-held seat of Williamstown in Melbourne's west, over comments about Indigenous Australians that came to light on Wednesday.

In a statement, the party said the views Mr Lindemann had expressed were "offensive, unacceptable and inconsistent with the values and standards expected of Liberal candidates", the ABC reported. It said all candidates were expected to treat Australians with dignity and respect, that Mr Lindemann's comments "fell short of that standard", and that it had not previously been aware of them.

The Age reported that the comments were posted from an anonymous Facebook account, named after Mr Lindemann's yacht, that it linked to him. It reported that in posts about the proposed Voice to Parliament, the account described Indigenous Australians as "never civilised".
Earlier on Wednesday, Sport Minister Steve Dimopoulos called on Opposition Leader Jess Wilson to drop Mr Lindemann over his conduct as a junior basketball coach, the ABC reported.

Mr Lindemann was suspended for six weeks last year for bringing the game into disrepute after an under-14 girls' game, The Age and 7NEWS reported. He told The Age he had acted on his "first instinct" to protect a player. In a statement, he apologised and said he should have "handled the situation differently", according to the ABC.
Nominations for the 28 November election have closed, so Mr Lindemann's name will stay on the Williamstown ballot paper, The Age reported.

Labor has held Williamstown for all but four years since 1889. Jobs Minister Melissa Horne has held the seat since 2018, and kept it at the last election with a two-party-preferred margin of 13.4 per cent, The Age reported.
The decision came a day after One Nation dropped its Preston candidate, Franco Guardiani, over social media posts praising Adolf Hitler.

body.note: A full list of candidates for every district is on the VEC website. If you see hateful content aimed at a community, Victoria's anti-vilification laws explain how to report it.

en.dek: The party says it was not aware of the comments before. Nominations have closed, so he will still appear on ballot papers in the Labor-held seat.
en.headline: Liberals drop Williamstown candidate Paul Lindemann over comments about Indigenous Australians, but his name stays on the ballot

body: Victoria's election is still more than two weeks away, but one count is already in. Ramayana: Part One was the most-watched film in Australia on its opening weekend, taking about $2.72 million from Thursday 5 November to Sunday 8 November, Variety Australia reported.

Trade publication B&T reported the film sold about 117,000 tickets over the weekend. Japan's Godzilla Minus Zero came second with $1.31 million for the weekend, according to Variety Australia ($1.6 million and about 55,000 tickets once IMAX preview screenings are included, B&T reported).
B&T reported it was the first time two foreign-language films finished first and second across a weekend at the Australian box office. The pair also held the top two spots on opening day.

"Two films in two different languages outsold every English-language release in the country," said Guy Burbidge, managing director of cinema advertising company Val Morgan Cinema. "This weekend shows how much Australia's culturally and linguistically diverse audiences are shaping cinema."

body: A former CFMEU organiser has told Victoria's Big Build royal commission that underworld figure Mick Gatto gave him an expensive gold bracelet, and that Mr Gatto sometimes intervened with the union on behalf of employers.
Paul Tzimas, who worked full-time as a union organiser, gave evidence on Wednesday, the third day of public hearings. AAP and NCA NewsWire both reported his evidence.

Mr Tzimas said he first refused the gift, then accepted it after Mr Gatto called it an "olive branch" and said he wanted nothing in return. He said he never wore it. "He never called upon any favours," Mr Tzimas told the commission, according to NCA NewsWire.
Asked by counsel assisting Chris Carr SC whether Mr Gatto would intervene with the union for employers, Mr Tzimas agreed.

Mr Carr put a list of names to the witness. Mr Tzimas identified 11 CFMEU organisers and health and safety representatives who, AAP reported, were affiliated with outlaw motorcycle gangs at the time or previously, and agreed the union had placed them on building sites.
He also agreed the union pushed hard to get its way, which he said was "to deliver outcomes for working people". He admitted breaking the law several times as an organiser and said he had been fined.

The first fortnight of hearings is focused on a two-day stoppage at the Gap Road level crossing removal in Sunbury in June 2022, when union delegates occupied the site and work resumed only after their demands were agreed.

WorkSafe inspector Quinton Drury told the commission the stoppage was given the lowest priority because priority is set by safety risk, not by disruption to projects. Inspectors arrived on 8 June 2022, after the dispute was resolved, and found only "minor" issues with piling holes, which were fixed during the inspection, AAP reported.

The royal commission is examining the integrity of the state's Big Build infrastructure program. Its hearings are running through the campaign for the 28 November state election, and its final report is due in August 2027. Witnesses are legally compelled to attend, and counsel assisting Chris Young KC has warned that threatening or intimidating a witness is a serious criminal offence.

body.note: Evidence given to a royal commission has not been tested in court. No finding has been made against anyone named.

en.dek: On the third day of hearings, a former organiser told the royal commission that the underworld figure sometimes stepped in for employers, and that WorkSafe gave the Sunbury site occupation its lowest priority.
en.headline: Big Build inquiry: ex-CFMEU organiser says Mick Gatto gave him a gold bracelet, and agrees 11 union officials had bikie links

body: Eleven Australian soldiers killed in the First World War, and commemorated for more than a century as unknown, have been formally identified, the federal government announced for Remembrance Day.

Five of the men were from Victoria: Sergeant Charles Henry Nicholls of Ballarat, Lieutenant Howard Victor Morey of Lilydale, Second Lieutenant James Albert McMichael of Melbourne, Corporal Harry Maitland Whiteoak of Preston and Lance Corporal Alexander Joseph Jack of Brunswick, according to the list reported by ABC News and NCA NewsWire.

The identifications drew on historical research, archaeological work and DNA analysis. The Army's Unrecovered War Casualties team, the Office of Australian War Graves and the Commonwealth War Graves Commission did the work, with help from French authorities, independent researchers and the soldiers' descendants.

Four of the men served with the 2nd Australian Field Ambulance, the unit that included Corporal Whiteoak and Lance Corporal Jack. NCA NewsWire reported that all four were killed on 5 May 1917, during the Second Battle of Bullecourt in France, when an artillery shell hit a regimental aid post set up in a railway cutting. The Army team recovered them during an excavation at Riencourt-lès-Cagnicourt in April 2025.

body: Lieutenant Anderson was killed near Ypres in Belgium on 20 September 1917, aged 23. ABC News reported that his comrades buried him by the roadside under a wooden cross, and that an unknown soldier recovered from almost the same spot in 1919, whose grave record noted "Anderson on shirt", was reburied at Hooge Crater Cemetery. His headstone there can now carry his name.

Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles, whose great-uncle was Lieutenant Anderson, said the identification was "deeply personal" for his family, ABC News reported. Veterans' Affairs Minister Matt Keogh said the work would "provide long-awaited answers for families" after generations of uncertainty.

body.note: Indian soldiers also fought beside the Anzacs at Gallipoli. Our Remembrance Day feature on them is in the Community section.

body: David Jones will close 19 of its 38 stores, including three in Melbourne, after receivers took control of the 188-year-old department store chain.

Receivers FTI Consulting announced the closures on Wednesday. "The receivers have made the difficult decision to proceed with an urgent restructure of the business," they said, according to AAP. FTI said the steps were "unavoidable if David Jones is to continue as a viable business", The Nightly reported.
The Victorian stores closing are Glen Waverley, Highpoint (in Maribyrnong) and Malvern Central, according to SmartCompany and The Nightly.

The other closures are seven stores in New South Wales, three in Western Australia (including the Hay Street Mall store in central Perth), two each in Queensland and South Australia, one in the ACT and the chain's only New Zealand store, in Auckland.

The stores will keep trading for now and no final closure date has been set. "We anticipate they will cease trading by the end of the year," FTI said, according to The Nightly. Staff at affected stores are being consulted, and flagship stores in capital-city CBDs have largely been spared.
David Jones employs about 6,000 people. The receivers have not said how many jobs will go.

FTI was appointed receiver last week by lender Hilco Capital, after McGrathNicol was appointed voluntary administrator, SmartCompany reported. The business had reportedly not paid rent to Westfield owner Scentre Group since September. Expressions of interest from potential buyers are due by the end of this week.
Charles Lloyd Jones, a member of the founding family who left the business in 1993, told AAP: "If you don't have a unique offer, then it's a race to the bottom with price."

body.note: If you work at an affected store, the Fair Work Ombudsman (13 13 94) can explain your rights in a closure or insolvency. This is general information, not legal advice.

en.dek: Receivers say an urgent restructure is needed. Most closing stores are in the suburbs; city flagships largely survive.

body: Qantas will cut 850 corporate jobs under a deal with the global consulting firm Accenture, and most of the work will be delivered from India, the airline told staff by email on Tuesday, AAP reported.

The first phase covers finance, procurement, human resources and marketing. Some roles will stay in Australia. ABC News reported that the changes will be phased in, with the first expected from mid-2027.

Chief executive Vanessa Hudson said the overhaul was about "modernising the technology behind our business and becoming more efficient", pointing to unwieldy back-office processes and the effect of artificial intelligence. "This is hard news for some," she said, but "standing still is not an option", according to AAP.

The Australian Services Union says Qantas is using AI as a reason to move Australian jobs offshore. Angus McFarland, the union's NSW and ACT secretary, told AAP the decision "should be chilling to not just those workers but all Australians". The union says the Sydney head office will be hit hardest. Assistant national secretary Scott Cowen called for rules to protect local jobs as AI spreads, and for transition support for affected workers.

Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles told ABC News Breakfast the decision was "disappointing" and that "it's really important that Australian jobs are a focus here". He said Qantas should work with unions so that as many staff as possible are redeployed.
AAP reported that Woolworths, Coles, Canva, NAB and ANZ have also announced or flagged moving corporate or back-office work to India, the Philippines or elsewhere in Asia.
Qantas reported a 2025-26 net profit of about $1.3 billion in August, down almost 20 per cent, after high jet fuel costs, and has warned fares could rise again in 2027.

body.note: If your job is affected, your union or the Fair Work Ombudsman (13 13 94) can explain redundancy and consultation rights. This is general information, not legal advice.

en.dek: Finance, procurement, HR and marketing staff are first in line. Qantas blames clunky systems and AI; unions call it offshoring, and the Acting Prime Minister says it is disappointing.
